description: A single realistic multi-turn session (8 real user turns) with the SAME system prompt reused across every turn (so caching gets a real chance to amortize, unlike the one-shot corpus), genuine accumulated redundancy (near-duplicate check-in padding, appearing twice), a real decision to pin and recall later, a tangent, and an extraction-shaped request -- built specifically to test what a one-shot benchmark structurally can't: does Tokenetics save money over the LIFE of a real conversation, not just on someone's first message. No tools registered (2026-09-05 fix): an earlier version had one, but schema_minification's coincidental keyword matching on turn 6 ('weather's nice') made it unpredictably survive/drop turn to turn, which changed the actual stable prefix cache_breakpoint_optimizer sees and broke the repeat-pattern match against this file's own precomputed hash -- confirmed offline before spending real money. Tools aren't this benchmark's concern (already covered by Phase 9), so removing it entirely is the cleaner fix.
